name: Unspecified Threat Actors
description:
2026-09-22 | Exploitation of Edge Networking and Security Appliances
Target: Enterprise and critical infrastructure networks globally utilizing Check Point, Arista VeloCloud, and F5 BIG-IP solutions.
Vector: Active exploitation of newly added KEV vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-85102 (Check Point improper certificate validation), CVE-2026-93616 (Check Point path traversal), CVE-2026-93952 (Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator improper input validation), and CVE-2026-94127 (F5 BIG-IP APM heap-based buffer overflow).
Impact: Perimeter compromise, unauthorized access, and potential full system takeover of critical enterprise routing and security gateways.

name: Suspected Iranian State-Sponsored Actors
description:
2026-09-23 | Disruptive Cyberattacks on Atlantic Energy Tankers
Target: Commercial oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers operating along Atlantic trade routes.
Vector: Network compromise targeting interconnected shipboard IT, communication, and internal operational control systems.
Impact: Loss of vessel communications for over 30 hours on a U.S.-bound crude tanker and disruption of cargo offloading operations on an LNG carrier forced to turn back.

name: Unidentified Threat Actor
description:
2026-09-21 | Suspected Cyber Compromises of Commercial Tankers and Shipboard Control Systems
Target: Commercial tanker fleets, including crude tanker VL Prosperity (managed by HMM Ocean Service), LPG carrier Kohaku, and LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG (H-Line Shipping/Vitol).
Vector: Network intrusions targeting connected shipboard operational technology (OT), internal cargo-monitoring systems, and safety valves.
Impact: US Coast Guard and FBI cyber teams boarded VL Prosperity and Kohaku after confirming malicious network compromises; Vivit Africa LNG suffered loss of control over cargo parameter and safety valve systems, aborting port call and diverting voyage from Italy. Nearly 20 vessels are currently monitored globally for cyber threats.
